title: Light Flash
description: A light flash transition is a brief blowout of the frame to white or near-white, then a return, as if a bulb, explosion, or memory dump hit the emulsion. It is a temporal event, often a cut hidden in the peak, not a standing lens flare.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The picture goes. For a few frames there is only density failure: a bulb, a muzzle, a Polaroid, a trauma.
Then the next image, or the same room, settles back. The flash is both a wound and a splice.
Use it when the cut should hurt: memory stings, explosions, still cameras in a crowd, a mind skipping. The white is the edit.
It is the wrong tool for a sun ghost that stays in shot, or for a smash cut that is only a hard join of two dark images. If the flare hangs and tracks a lamp, that is flare.
If you simply jump scenes with no blowout, that is a smash cut.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Overexpose a practical, a strobe, or a muzzle until clipping, or animate a white frame at the cut. Recovery can carry a lingering veil.
In camera, a still photographer's flash or a door onto daylight can do it live. Prompt: frame going to white then returning, bulb or explosion or memory sting, not a persistent source-linked flare.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: A hard flash blows out a face, then settles into the next memory, as in a sting cut. Do not leave a decorative streak parked on the lens after the white is gone.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Smash Cut is an abrupt edit without a required white-out. A light flash is the white that can carry that cut.
Lens Flare is scatter that remains while a source is in the optic. Fade In / Fade Out goes slowly to black or white as a chapter mark.
A flash is fast. Iris closes a circle.
It does not blow the whole field.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Memento uses white flashes as memory dumps between Polaroids and the present. Saving Private Ryan lets muzzle flashes and overload wipe the frame as combat sting.
Raging Bull's camera flashes in the ring are the still-photographer version of the same blowout.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Wrong cousin: persistent lens flare or a smash cut with no exposure event. Tell: a rainbow streak that never whites the frame, or a hard cut in full detail.
Fix: clip to white (or near-white) for frames, then recover. Hide the splice in the peak if it is a transition.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is a light flash in film?
A brief blowout of the image to white, then a return, used as a sting or as a cut. It is overexposure as an event, not a standing artifact.
Light flash vs lens flare
Flare is stray light in the optic that can last as long as the source is in play. A light flash is a temporal wipe of the frame, often covering an edit.
When should I use a light flash?
When a cut or a shock should be a wound of light: memory, explosion, still-camera flash. Do not use it as decoration on a quiet master.
How do I prompt a light flash for AI image or video?
For video, describe a blowout to white and a settle-back, and name the cause (bulb, muzzle, memory). For stills, show the peak or the recovery, not a parked streak.
